title: Sick in Cabo? What to Do and What It Costs (2026 Guide)
description: Got sick in Cabo San Lucas? Step-by-step guide for US travelers: when to call 911, house-call doctors ($199), IV hydration, pharmacy delivery and insurance.

intro: Getting sick on vacation is stressful — especially in another country. The good news: Los Cabos has excellent private medical care, and for most vacation illnesses you do not need to leave your hotel or villa. This guide walks you through exactly what to do, in order, with real prices in US dollars.
If anyone has chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, a seizure, heavy bleeding or is unresponsive, call 911 now. Everything below is for urgent but non-life-threatening situations.

sections.h2: Step 1: Decide how urgent it is
p: Most vacation illnesses in Cabo fall into a few groups: stomach bugs and food poisoning, dehydration and heat exhaustion, sunburn, ear and throat infections, urinary tract infections, colds and flu, allergic reactions and minor injuries. These are exactly the cases a house-call doctor handles in your room.
list: Call 911 / go to a hospital — chest pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, fainting, severe bleeding, a high fever with a stiff neck, or a serious injury.
Call a house-call doctor today — fever, vomiting or diarrhea that will not stop, painful urination, ear pain, a rash, a sprain or a cut that may need stitches.
IV hydration — when you cannot keep fluids down, feel dizzy or weak after a stomach bug, too much sun or a long night out.
Pharmacy delivery — when you already know what you need: rehydration salts, pain relievers, allergy medication, sunscreen or a refill.

sections.h2: Step 2: Get a doctor to your room
p: In Los Cabos, English-speaking doctors make house calls to hotels, villas, Airbnbs and yachts, day and night. With Pharmacy & Doctors, a doctor visit at your location is $199 USD, or $99 USD at our downtown Cabo San Lucas clinic. Typical arrival is 30–45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas and the Tourist Corridor, and up to about 60 minutes in San José del Cabo.
Your hotel front desk can also call its on-call doctor. Either way, ask the price before the visit — a reputable provider will tell you up front.
p_after: Book on our house-call doctor page or message us on WhatsApp with your location and symptoms.

sections.h2: Step 3: Rehydrate — with an IV if you need it
p: Dehydration is the most common reason a vacation day goes sideways in Cabo: hot sun, alcohol, long flights and stomach bugs all add up. If you can sip fluids, oral rehydration salts from any pharmacy work well. If you cannot keep anything down, a nurse-administered IV drip at your hotel rehydrates you in about 45–60 minutes.
Our IV drips are $159–$189.99 USD + tax at your door, $129–$159 + tax at our clinic, and $119 per person, tax included for groups of 6 or more. See the full IV menu.

Mexican pharmacies stock most of what you use at home, often under different brand names. Antibiotics require a prescription in Mexico — a doctor visit takes care of that. We deliver medications and pharmacy essentials to your room 24/7, usually in 30–45 minutes, with free delivery on orders over $50 USD. More on pharmacy delivery.

sections.h2: Step 5: Keep your paperwork for travel insurance
p: Most US health plans cover little or nothing in Mexico, but travel medical insurance usually reimburses doctor visits, IV therapy prescribed by a doctor and medications. Ask for an itemized invoice in English and USD — we provide one at every visit — and photograph your receipts. Call your insurer's assistance line before any hospital admission.

Pack a list of your medications (generic names) and allergies.
Save a local 24/7 doctor's WhatsApp number — ours is +52 624 226 1023.
Bring oral rehydration salts, sunscreen and any prescription you need for the whole trip.

faq.q: Can a doctor come to my hotel in Cabo San Lucas?
faq.a: Yes. English-speaking doctors make house calls to hotels, villas, Airbnbs and yachts 24/7. With Pharmacy & Doctors the visit is $199 USD, and typical arrival is 30 to 45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas.

faq.q: How much does a doctor visit cost in Cabo?
faq.a: A house call from Pharmacy & Doctors is $199 USD at your hotel or villa, or $99 USD at our downtown clinic. Ask any provider for the price before the visit.

faq.q: Does my US health insurance work in Mexico?
faq.a: Usually not for routine care. Travel medical insurance typically reimburses doctor visits and medications. Keep the itemized invoice and receipts and submit them to your insurer.

faq.q: Can I get antibiotics at a pharmacy in Cabo?
faq.a: Antibiotics require a prescription in Mexico. A doctor can evaluate you and prescribe them if appropriate, and we can deliver the medication to your room.

faq.q: What number do I call for an emergency in Mexico?
faq.a: Call 911. It works nationwide, including Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo.
